lessons.title: Plans, permission, and unreal conditions: можно, нельзя, если бы
lessons.explanation: This final lesson adds three devices that hold a long conversation together: permission, plans, and unreal conditions. Permission centres on можно and нельзя. Можно войти? (MOZH-na vay-TEE) — may I come in? asks for permission, and нельзя refuses or prohibits it. Neither takes a nominative subject, so if you name the person concerned you use the dative, exactly as with надо: Мне нельзя вставать (mnye NYEL-zya fsta-VAT) — I am not allowed to get up, a sentence the sources put in a doctor's mouth. Aspect does real work here too. Cornell contrasts Тут нельзя переходить улицу (toot NYEL-zya pee-ree-kha-DEET OO-lee-tsoo) — you cannot cross the street here, a general prohibition expressed with the imperfective, against Сейчас нельзя перейти улицу — you cannot cross the street right now, a one-off impossibility expressed with the perfective. Plans use собираться plus an infinitive or a perfective future, and they also use the two-verbs-in-a-row pattern: После обеда я пойду куплю сыр (POS-le a-BYE-da ya pay-DOO koop-LYOO syr) — after dinner I will go and buy cheese, where the first verb of motion carries the future and the second, also perfective and non-past, names the purpose. Unreal conditions use the particle бы with the past-tense form of the verb in both halves of the sentence: Если бы у меня были деньги, я бы поехала в Москву (YES-lee by oo mee-NYA BY-lee DYEN-gee, ya by pa-YE-kha-la v mask-VOO) — if I had money, I would go to Moscow. Spanish offers an interesting contrast, because Spanish distinguishes si tuviera from si hubiera tenido and iría from habría ido, while Russian uses one and the same form for hypothetical and contrary-to-fact conditions and leaves the difference to context.
lessons.example: Hold a four-turn conversation about a weekend and label each turn. — Что ты собираешься делать в выходные? (shto ty sa-bee-RA-yesh-sya DYE-lat v vy-khad-NY-ye) — what are you planning to do at the weekend? — Я собираюсь поехать к родителям (ya sa-bee-RA-yus pa-YE-khat k ra-DEE-tye-lyam) — I am planning to go to my parents, with собираться plus a perfective infinitive and к plus the dative for the people visited. — А можно с тобой? (a MOZH-na s ta-BOY) — may I come with you?, where с plus the instrumental marks company and можно asks permission. — Конечно, но мне надо купить билеты (ka-NYESH-na, no mnye NA-da koo-PEET bee-LYE-ty) — of course, but I have to buy tickets, a dative obligation. Then add a regret to show the conditional: Если бы билеты были дешевле, я бы ездила чаще (YES-lee by bee-LYE-ty BY-lee dee-SHEV-lye, ya by YEZ-dee-la CHA-shche) — if tickets were cheaper, I would travel more often. Read the five turns with the stress marks, then say them at normal conversational speed, naming each turn's device: plan, plan, permission, obligation, unreal condition.
lessons.question: Why can Если бы у меня были деньги, я бы поехала в Москву mean both 'if I had money, I would go to Moscow' and 'if I had had money, I would have gone to Moscow'?
lessons.answer: Russian forms unreal conditions with бы plus the past-tense form in both halves and therefore uses one shape for hypothetical and contrary-to-fact meaning, leaving the difference to context.
lessons.distractor: The form is past tense throughout, so only the contrary-to-fact reading is possible, and the hypothetical reading needs a different particle.
lessons.correction: The л-form used with бы is a mood marker rather than a tense marker: Cornell states plainly that since there is no choice of forms, the learner does not have to worry about past, present, or future, or about hypothetical versus contrary-to-fact, and that English distinguishes the two types while Russian does not. Two practical rules follow. The particle бы cannot stand first in its clause, so it clings to the word after the opening conjunction or pronoun. And бы must not be equated with English would, which in reported speech can translate a plain future, as in Он сказал, что придёт.

depth.definitions: Permission is expressed by the predicatives можно and нельзя, its negative; both are subjectless and take a dative person when one is named. No necessity means you may refrain: Cornell gives не обязательно, or a form of мочь with не placed before the infinitive, as in Ты можешь не покупать их сегодня. An unreal condition is a sentence of the if-then type in which the premise is hypothetical or contrary to fact, formed in Russian with бы plus the л-form in both clauses. A real condition uses если with ordinary tenses, as in Если он придёт, мы поедем за город. Собираться means to intend and takes an infinitive. The two-verbs-in-a-row pattern joins a perfective motion verb with a second perfective verb naming the purpose.
depth.mechanism: The permission and obligation constructions share one mechanism, namely the removal of the nominative subject: Russian states a permitted or prohibited action as a general fact about a situation, and the person involved is added in the dative if mentioned at all. Cornell's page on можно and нельзя adds the aspect rule that makes the construction usable, distinguishing a general prohibition in the street from an immediate impossibility now, and it notes that нельзя is the negative of можно because нельзя is a separate word rather than можно plus не. Unreal conditions work differently again: the particle бы converts the past-tense form into a mood marker, and the constraint that it cannot open a clause is a genuine word-order rule the sources state explicitly. Two honest limitations belong here. First, the ambiguity between hypothetical and contrary-to-fact is resolved by context, so a beginner may produce a sentence that is grammatically perfect and still ambiguous, which is normal rather than a failure. Second, permission in conversation is often handled by intonation and by set phrases such as Можно? and Пожалуйста, so no verb at all may appear.
depth.secondExample: Compare a real condition, an unreal condition, and a permission refusal on the same topic. Real: Если у меня будет время, я поеду в Москву (YES-lee oo mee-NYA BOO-det VRYE-mya, ya pa-YE-doo v mask-VOO) — if I have time, I will go to Moscow, with a perfective future in each clause. Unreal: Если бы у меня было время, я бы поехала в Москву — if I had time or had had time, I would go or would have gone to Moscow, with бы plus the л-form twice. Refusal of permission: Мне нельзя ехать в Москву (mnye NYEL-zya YE-khat v mask-VOO) — I am not allowed to go to Moscow, a subjectless prohibition with the person in the dative. The three sentences describe overlapping situations and share only one word, поехать. Comparing them side by side is the fastest way to feel the difference between what is likely, what is contrary to fact, and what is permitted.
depth.mistake: Four errors recur. The first puts бы in first position, producing Бы если у меня были деньги, which violates the word-order constraint. The second uses a conditional form where a real condition is meant, or the reverse, so an ordinary plan sounds like a fantasy; the test is whether the speaker treats the premise as likely. The third uses можно plus не for a prohibition, as in Можно не курить? when the meaning is that smoking is not permitted; the correct prohibition is Здесь нельзя курить. The fourth names the person in the nominative with a predicative, as in Я нельзя вставать instead of Мне нельзя вставать. Diagnose by classifying the sentence first: permission, prohibition, no-necessity, real condition, or unreal condition, and only then assembling the pieces.
depth.application: Optional practice, and the natural close of the level: write a six-turn dialogue in which two people arrange an outing, using at least one plan with собираться, one request with можно, one prohibition with нельзя, one obligation with надо, one real condition with если, and one unreal condition with если бы. Model response for two turns: — Можно я приеду в субботу? — Конечно, если ты не забудешь билеты; если бы они были дешевле, я бы ездила каждую неделю (MOZH-na ya pree-YE-doo f soo-BO-too? ka-NYESH-na, YES-lee ty nye za-BOO-desh bee-LYE-ty; YES-lee by a-NEE BY-lee dee-SHEV-lye, ya by YEZ-dee-la KAZH-doo-yoo nee-DYE-lyoo) — may I come on Saturday? Of course, if you do not forget the tickets; if they were cheaper, I would travel every week. Self-review checks four things: every device from the list appears at least once, permission and obligation sentences keep the person in the dative where required, real conditions use ordinary tenses and unreal ones use бы plus the л-form, and бы never opens a clause. Read the dialogue aloud twice, once labelling each device and once as a conversation.
depth.summary: Permission, prohibition, no-necessity, obligation, plans, and conditions are all built by combining a small number of predicative words, the dative, and the particle бы. Можно and нельзя keep the person in the dative and use aspect to separate a general permission from a one-off impossibility; собираться and the two-verbs-in-a-row pattern carry plans; and бы plus the л-form expresses hypothetical and contrary-to-fact conditions with a single shape. Spanish distinguishes conditional and perfect conditional forms where Russian does not, so context, not morphology, resolves the difference.

It gives the aspect contrast between Тут нельзя переходить улицу and Сейчас нельзя перейти улицу, states that нельзя is the negative of можно, and shows the dative with a named person in Врач сказал, что мне нельзя вставать. Use it to extend the dialogue task beyond one errand; the page's own Cyrillic renders with legacy stress glyphs, so read the structure rather than the accents.

It confirms independently that the conditional is formed by adding бы to a past-tense form, that the particle follows the word marking the supposed subject, and that the masculine and feminine forms differ, as in я бы сказал against я бы сказала. Encyclopaedia-level confirmation, not a teaching sequence.

visual.title: Which device, which case
visual.description: A labelled sequence for assembling a conversational turn that expresses a plan, a permission, or a condition without mixing their grammars.
steps: Classify the turn: plan, permission, prohibition, no-necessity, obligation, real condition, or unreal condition.
For a plan, use собираться plus an infinitive or the two-verbs-in-a-row pattern with a perfective motion verb first.
For permission or prohibition, use можно or нельзя, name the person in the dative if you name one, and choose aspect: imperfective for a general rule, perfective for a one-off situation.
For no-necessity, use не надо with care, or better, можешь не plus an imperfective infinitive, or не обязательно.
For a real condition, use если with ordinary tenses, at least one clause in a perfective future.
For an unreal condition, use the л-form in both clauses with бы, placed after the first word and never first in the clause.
Say the turn aloud and name the device, then check that every named person is nominative or dative as that device requires.

questions.prompt: A learner describes a daily routine and writes Каждый день я иду на работу пешком. What must change, and does the transport phrase change with it?
questions.answer: The verb must become the multi-directional ходить: Каждый день я хожу на работу пешком, while the phrase пешком stays exactly as it is.
questions.distractor: Both the verb and the transport phrase must change, giving Каждый день я езжу на работу на машине, since a routine always takes the vehicle pair.
questions.correction: Habitual motion is what selects the multi-directional verb, and on-foot habit selects ходить; the adverb пешком is not tied to either verb in the pair but to the manner of movement, so it does not change. The vehicle pair would be wrong here because пешком states explicitly that no vehicle is involved. The one part of the sentence that must change is the verb's shape, not its meaning.

questions.prompt: You are standing outside a building and want to know how to get to the metro. Write the question and explain why that prefix and preposition are used rather than the pair meaning 'enter'.
questions.answer: Как дойти до метро? uses до- with до plus the genitive because the question asks how to reach a place, not how to go inside one.
questions.distractor: Как войти в метро? is the natural question, because asking directions always uses the entering verb with в plus the accusative.
questions.correction: Войти means to enter an enclosed space and presupposes that you are already at its threshold, which is not what someone asking for directions needs. До- plus до and the genitive expresses reaching a point, and the sources use exactly this pattern in directions such as telling someone to go as far as the second traffic light. The distinction is about the path, so the prefix and the preposition must be chosen together.

questions.prompt: Describe the room you are in: say where a cup, a book, and a cat are, using the right position verb and case for each.
questions.answer: На столе стоит чашка, на столе лежит книга, на диване сидит кошка, because the cup has a base, the book lies flat, the cat is a living being, and location takes в or на plus the prepositional.
questions.distractor: На столе лежит чашка, на столе лежит книга, на диване лежит кошка, because лежать is the neutral verb for an object occupying a place.
questions.correction: Лежать is only neutral for objects without a base; a cup rests on its bottom, so Russian treats it as standing, and a living creature sits rather than lies. The bases differ per object, which is why the rule of thumb rather than the object's material decides the verb. The case is separate from the verb choice: all three sentences answer где and therefore take the prepositional.

questions.prompt: A friend is arriving at your flat and you want to tell her to sit on the sofa, then add that she will need to take off her shoes. Write both and justify the aspect of the command.
questions.answer: Сядьте на диван uses a perfective command for one specific act, and Тебе надо снять обувь expresses the second part as a dative obligation with надо and an infinitive.
questions.distractor: Садитесь на диван uses a perfective form for the specific act, and Ты надо снять обувь expresses the obligation.
questions.correction: Садитесь is the imperfective invitation and сядьте the perfective instruction, so the distractor reverses the aspect labels while also putting the person in the nominative with надо. The obligation requires the dative: тебе надо. Choose the aspect by asking whether you are inviting someone to settle in or directing one completed movement, and choose the case by asking which construction, subjectless or subject-centred, you are using.

questions.prompt: Two colleagues are arranging a trip. Write a two-turn exchange in which one asks for permission to join and the other mentions an obligation, then add one unreal condition about the same trip.
questions.answer: Можно с вами? — Конечно, но мне надо купить билеты; если бы билеты были дешевле, мы бы поехали раньше.
questions.distractor: Можно я с вами? — Конечно, но я надо купить билеты; если билеты были дешевле, мы поехали раньше.
questions.correction: The permission question is fine with or without я, but the obligation cannot put the person in the nominative with надо: the dative мне is required. The unreal condition needs the particle бы in both clauses, and it may not open the clause, so если бы билеты были дешевле must be followed by мы бы поехали раньше. Compare the real condition, which would read если билеты будут дешевле, мы поедем раньше, with ordinary future forms and no бы at all.

questions.prompt: It is your mother's birthday. In one spoken paragraph, say that you bought her a present, paid by card, and showed her the photographs you took on your phone. Then state which four endings you had to choose and what each one marks.
questions.answer: Я купила маме подарок и заплатила картой, а потом показала ей фотографии, которые сняла телефоном. The endings are the dative маме and ей for the recipient, the accusative подарок and фотографии for the things, and the instrumentals картой and телефоном for the means, with no prepositions at all.
questions.distractor: Я купила маму подарком и заплатила с картой, а потом показала её фотографиям, которые сняла с телефоном. The endings are the accusative маму for the recipient, the instrumental подарком for the thing, and с plus the instrumental for the means.
questions.correction: The roles are assigned by the verbs, not by the surface order: купить puts the person in the dative and the thing in the accusative, платить takes a bare instrumental for the means, показать keeps the recipient dative and the thing accusative, and снимать takes a bare instrumental for the instrument. Spanish le compré a mamá and con tarjeta would suggest two separate prepositional words, and Russian has none, which is exactly the trap the distractor illustrates. A further point worth noticing is that the same person can appear in two different cases if her roles differ: as a recipient she is маме or ей, and as the thing acted on she would be маму, which is why the role must be decided before the ending.

questions.prompt: Write four sentences that describe a difficult morning: that you were cold, that you needed a hot drink, that you did not want to get up, and that you are now bored. Use the impersonal frames and justify every agreeing word.
questions.answer: Утром мне было холодно; мне был нужен горячий чай; мне не хотелось вставать; сейчас мне скучно. The agreeing words are the neuter past было and the masculine short form нужен, which follows чай.
questions.distractor: Утром я была холодная; мне нужно горячий чай; я не хотелась вставать; сейчас я скучная. The agreeing words follow the speaker, who is the subject of every sentence.
questions.correction: In dative impersonals there is no nominative subject, so nothing can agree with the speaker: было is the fixed neuter past of быть, and нужен agrees with the thing needed rather than with the person needing it. The distractor makes the speaker a subject throughout, which is the single most common Spanish-influenced error in this construction, since Spanish tengo frío and estoy aburrida both put the person in subject position. The fourth sentence, сейчас мне скучно, is genuinely subjectless and takes no agreeing word at all.

questions.prompt: A classmate writes Я шла в школу с ручкой и с подругой. Both noun phrases look identical in structure but only one is about company in the ordinary sense. Explain what the sentence means, whether it is grammatical, and how you would rewrite it if you meant that you write with a pen.
questions.answer: The sentence is grammatical and means I was walking to school with a pen and with a friend, since с plus the instrumental marks accompaniment for both nouns. To express the pen as an instrument, the preposition must disappear: Я пишу ручкой.
questions.distractor: The sentence is ungrammatical because с plus the instrumental can only mark a person, so the pen phrase must be rewritten as Я шла в школу с ручкой in the genitive.
questions.correction: С plus the instrumental marks accompaniment with people and things alike, which is why с ручкой can only mean with a pen in your possession, and why the sentence is not ungrammatical but simply says something odd. The instrument sense belongs to the bare instrumental, as lesson 63 showed with Я пишу ручкой against Я ем суп со сметаной. The genitive after с would mean from or off, which is a third meaning entirely, as in Книга упала со стола.

questions.prompt: Narrate one day of travel in four sentences using four different members of the motion family: one habit, one motion in progress, one plan, and one completed round trip. Then explain what each choice asserts that the others would not.
questions.answer: Я обычно хожу на работу пешком; вчера, когда я шла туда, я встретила друга; завтра я пойду на выставку; а в аптеку я уже сходила. The habit uses ходить, the motion in progress uses идти, the plan uses the perfective пойти, and the completed round trip uses the special perfective сходить.
questions.distractor: Я обычно иду на работу пешком; вчера, когда я ходила туда, я встретила друга; завтра я схожу на выставку; а в аптеку я уже пошла. The habit uses идти, the motion in progress uses ходить, the plan uses the с- perfective, and the completed trip uses по-.
questions.correction: Идти cannot express a habit because it reports one-directional motion at one moment, and ходить cannot express motion in progress at that moment; the distractor swaps exactly these two. The special perfective with с- reports a trip that has been completed and returned from, so it cannot be the form you use when announcing a plan, and по- cannot report a finished round trip. The four labels, habit, in progress, plan, and completed trip, are what select the verb, and the choice is independent of distance and of means of transport.

questions.prompt: You are lost in an unfamiliar city. Write three sentences: one asking how to reach the railway station, one telling a companion to go as far as the traffic light, and one saying that you dropped in at a shop along the way. Then identify the prefix and the case in each.
questions.answer: Как дойти до вокзала?; Дойдите до светофора; по дороге я зашла в магазин. The first two use до- with до plus the genitive, and the third uses за- with в plus the accusative for the place entered.
questions.distractor: Как войти до вокзала?; Войдите до светофора; по дороге я вошла к магазину. The first two use в- with до plus the genitive, and the third uses в- with к plus the dative.
questions.correction: В- takes в plus the accusative and means entering an enclosed space, so it cannot be combined with до plus the genitive; the distractor mixes the prefix of one path with the preposition of another. За- with в plus the accusative reports a brief stop on the way, while за- with к plus the dative would report dropping in at a person's place, which is why the shop phrase needs в and not к. The direction cases are consistent: accusative for where to, genitive for where from or as far as, dative with к for a person visited.

questions.prompt: Describe your living room in three sentences: say where the lamp is, where the keys are, and where the cat is; then say in two further sentences that yesterday you put the lamp on the table and the keys in the bag. Account for every verb and case choice.
questions.answer: В комнате стоит лампа, на столе лежат ключи, а на диване сидит кошка; вчера я поставила лампу на стол и положила ключи в сумку. States take стоять, лежать, and сидеть with the prepositional after в or на, and the changes of position take the perfective поставить and положить with the accusative of destination.
questions.distractor: В комнате лежит лампа, на столе стоят ключи, а на диване лежит кошка; вчера я положила лампу на стола и поставила ключи в сумке. States are all expressed with лежать, and the changes take the genitive or prepositional of place.
questions.correction: The distractor applies лежать to everything, which fails on two counts: a lamp with a base stands, and a living creature sits. It also keeps the wrong case after the put-verbs, since a destination answers куда and takes the accusative, while the genitive would answer where from and the prepositional where at. Separately, the aspect contrast matters: the state verbs are imperfective reports of how things are, and the put-verbs are perfective reports of completed changes.

questions.prompt: Your neighbour knocks with her shoes on and pushes past you into the flat. Write two commands, one telling her to take off her shoes and one inviting her to sit down, and justify the aspect of each. Then explain what a perfective form would change in each case.
questions.answer: Снимите обувь, пожалуйста is a perfective instruction to complete one specific action, and садитесь, пожалуйста is an imperfective invitation to settle down; making the second perfective as сядьте would turn a welcome into a direction to one spot.
questions.distractor: Снимайте обувь, пожалуйста is a perfective instruction to complete one specific action, and сядьте, пожалуйста is an imperfective invitation to settle down; making the first imperfective would mean she must finish the action.
questions.correction: The distractor reverses the labels and therefore reverses the effects: снимайте is the imperfective, and an imperfective command in this situation asks her to get on with the process rather than to finish it, which is why hosts use imperfective forms for coats and perfective forms for specific instructions like taking off a shirt in a surgery. Aspect in commands tracks what the speaker wants done, not how polite the speaker feels; politeness is carried by пожалуйста, intonation, and the -те ending.

questions.prompt: Your colleague has offered to collect documents from the office. Write the same instruction in two ways, once with the person as a subject and once subjectless, then explain how a Russian speaker distinguishes I do not have to from you must not.
questions.answer: Ты должен забрать документы against Тебе надо забрать документы; the first has a nominative subject with the short adjective должен, the second a dative person with the predicative надо. Не надо is ambiguous between must not and need not, so the unambiguous no-necessity is Тебе не надо забирать or, better, Ты можешь не забирать.
questions.distractor: Ты надо забрать документы against Тебе должен забрать документы; the first is subjectless and the second has a subject. Не надо is always the unambiguous way to say you do not have to, so no alternative is needed.
questions.correction: The constructions cannot be cross-bred: должен agrees with a nominative subject and надо takes a dative person, so the distractor's two sentences are both malformed. On the negation, the sources state that не надо is ambiguous and usually read as must not or should not, while the clear expression of no necessity is a form of мочь with не before an imperfective infinitive, or the predicative не обязательно, which also works as a short answer. Keeping those two devices apart prevents a polite refusal from sounding like a prohibition.

questions.prompt: At a swimming pool, one sign reads Здесь нельзя прыгать. A guard tells you Вам нельзя прыгнуть с этой вышки. Explain why the two sentences use different verb forms and what each one means.
questions.answer: Both are prohibitions with the person or situation in question; the sign uses the imperfective because it states a general rule, while the guard uses the perfective because the impossibility applies to one specific occasion and one specific jump.
questions.distractor: The sign uses the perfective for a permanent rule, and the guard uses the imperfective because прыгать is the only form that can follow нельзя with a dative person.
questions.correction: The aspect labels are reversed in the distractor, and neither form is excluded by the presence of a dative person. The sources make the contrast explicit with a street-crossing pair: a general prohibition takes the imperfective, while an impossibility arising from the present situation takes the perfective. The same distinction carries over to any нельзя sentence, which is why reading a sign and hearing a warning about this jump now feel different in Russian even though English renders both with cannot.

questions.prompt: In a single paragraph, say that you would have gone to the coast if the tickets had been cheaper, but that you will nevertheless go next month if you can take leave, and that your friend says she will come. Use the correct conditional machinery and explain why two of the clauses look identical in form.
questions.answer: Если бы билеты были дешевле, я бы поехала на море; но в следующем месяце я поеду, если смогу взять отпуск; подруга сказала, что она приедет. The first half is unreal, with бы plus the л-form in both clauses; the second and third are real, using ordinary future forms.
questions.distractor: Если билеты были бы дешевле, я поехала на море; но в следующем месяце я бы поеду, если смогу взять отпуск; подруга сказала, что она бы приехала. The first half is unreal, and the reported speech takes бы because English says would come.
questions.correction: Three errors are packed into the distractor. The particle бы cannot be separated from the word it follows in the way the first clause shows, and it must appear in both clauses of an unreal condition. A real future cannot take бы, since бы marks unreality rather than politeness or futurity. And reported speech does not take бы for an English would that is really a future, which is exactly why Он сказал, что придёт has no particle at all; the sources warn against equating бы with English would on that specific ground.

questions.prompt: A friend is moving flat and needs help. Write a five-turn exchange in which you offer to come, ask what you must bring, ask permission to bring another person, hear a prohibition about the lift, and end with a plan naming a time. Then list the device used in each turn.
questions.answer: Я могу приехать в субботу; что мне надо взять; можно я приеду с братом; в лифте нельзя ставить коробки, придётся нести по лестнице; хорошо, я приеду к десяти и мы начнём с кухни. The turns use an offer, a dative obligation with надо, a permission request with можно plus с and the instrumental, a prohibition with нельзя, and a plan expressed with a perfective future.
questions.distractor: Я могу приехать в субботу; что я надо взять; можно я приеду с братом; в лифте нельзя ставить коробки; хорошо, я бы приеду к десяти и мы бы начали с кухни. The turns use an offer, an obligation, a permission request, a prohibition, and a conditional plan.
questions.correction: Two turns are broken in the distractor. The obligation cannot put the person in the nominative with надо, so что мне надо взять is the correct shape. The closing plan is a real arrangement with a fixed time, so it needs ordinary future forms, not the conditional with бы, which would turn a promise into a hypothetical. The permission request is correct as written, since с plus the instrumental marks the extra companion and можно asks leave; the prohibition keeps the dative-free impersonal shape typical of signs and rules.

questions.prompt: Read this account and repair it: Вчера я ходила в магазин, чтобы купить подарок. Я купила маме книгу и платила с картой. Потом я пришла с работы домой и положила книгу на столе. Identify each error, name the case or form that should stand instead, and explain the principle behind each repair.
questions.answer: The sentence is largely sound but three items need repair: платила should be заплатила for the completed payment, с картой should be картой because the card is the means rather than a companion, and на столе should be на стол because a put-verb takes the accusative of destination; ходила and купила are correct as a completed round trip and a completed purchase.
questions.distractor: Ходила should be шла because the trip was one-way, платила is correct as a completed payment, с картой is correct because с marks the instrument, and на столе is correct because the book is now on the table.
questions.correction: The distractor misreads the narrative in three places. Ходила is right because the trip is presented as a completed round trip rather than as motion in progress, and using шла would report being on the way. A completed payment takes the perfective заплатила, and the aspect of the earlier purchase, which the distractor leaves alone, is the clue: the whole account is a chain of completed events. The means of payment takes the bare instrumental, while с plus the instrumental would make the card a companion. Finally, the destination of положить answers куда and takes the accusative, even though the state sentence that follows, книга лежит на столе, takes the prepositional.
